entry.title: The wrinkles come back
entry.question: Do your bath wrinkles make a new pattern every time?
entry.answer: Some of the same lines return.
entry.explanation: Researchers photographed fingertips after two water soaks, at least a day apart. Major wrinkles reappeared in similar places and directions, even though the skin had returned to normal between sessions.
entry.qualification: A preliminary 2025 study of just three adults. Some wrinkles differed. It supports recurring patterns, not a perfectly identical map every time.
entry.whyCare: Something familiar on your own hands has a pattern you may never have noticed.

share.question: Do your bath wrinkles make a new pattern every time?
share.description: A small study found a recurring detail in water-wrinkled fingers.

evidence.scope: Three adults, ages 19–22; five right-hand fingers each.
evidence.denominator: Three people observed at two time points; repeated wrinkle measurements are not independent participants.
evidence.methodology: Laytin and German, §§2–3.3 and Figure 3. Two 30-minute immersions at 40°C, at least 24 hours apart. Researchers paired wrinkles and compared orientations. Exact calendar dates unspecified. Small sample and manual pairing limit generalization. No calculation; blood-vessel mapping remains a hypothesis.
